White Mountain Puzzles The Eighties - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:b94eac5104dc142a073b662ff11284e3]] I loved this amazing puzzle. The artwork is fantastic! This is a painting of a whole bunch of pictures and other scenes and people from the 1980's. It's based on a painting by Jim Mellet, and his art is amazing! It takes a ton of scenes and people from the 1980's, and turns it into a wonderful painted collage.

The quality of the puzzle is top-notch. The pieces are very thick, and so they fit together well. In my video, you can see that I can actually pick up the entire puzzle, which is usually impossible to do with most puzzles. The backing is a nice blue color, so you can easily tell which pieces are upside down. The border is awesome. The puzzle is surrounded by a red and orange line. This makes the border really easy to put together, and it makes it very easy to identify the edge pieces.

The puzzle is challenging, but it's also very doable. In most puzzles, there's a huge spot of the same color that's very boring, and this puzzle didn't have any of this. I felt entertained and challenged throughout. It's also a great conversation starter, because it has so many iconic people and scenes. I especially liked the Atari, Donkey Kong, Pac-Man, and Mr. T.

Pros:
+Challenging, yet doable
+Fun events and people from the 1980's
+Excellent artwork
+High quality puzzle

Cons:

Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11' Like many people, I have seen this product advertised on television and was excited to see if it is as fun as it looks in the commercials. The set comes with 1 car, a sheet of stickers to decorate the car, and 20 track segments in four different colors. The car requires 2 AAA batteries that are NOT included. The track segments are made of small individual pieces, which is why the box says it comes with 220 pieces of track.

The track is flexible and can be arranged in many different ways, and each segment can be used as a straight or curved part of the track. The car worked well and stayed on the track. A small pamphlet with quick trips is included with ideas on making the track more fun. I used the cardboard pieces used to package the car to create a small ramp and tunnel which worked better than I expected. After the track pieces were exposed to bright light, they did slightly glow in the dark. However, the box shows a picture of a looped track. I tried both a couple types of loops and none of them worked because the flexible track wouldn't support the weight of the car. In spite of this, this is a fun racetrack set that allows for a lot of different track formations to keep kids interested.
text_fidelity_b: Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11'

Barbie Made to Move Doll, Orange Top Made to Move Teresa (blue top) can be posed almost like a real person. So it’s great for people who use her for photography, or in place of an artist wooden mannequin for drawing.

Her face and thick eyebrows seem to be modeled after 1980’s actress and model Brooke Shields. If you’re buying her for a child, the downside is the delicate and sparse hair plugs that will easily be yanked with any vigorous brushing like children tend to do.

The flash lightens up her skin tone in photos. In reality she has a very tanned orangey skin color. The deep orange tint is strange like a bad fake tan, but I got used to it.

I like the 2015 version of her face more than the 2019 version: she had softer eyes, two defined dimples, a more realistic natural-looking mouth, and less of an orange skin. If you want the 2015 version you can get one used on ebay.

Overall it’s a good doll for collectors, photographers, and artists.

If you're looking for a Made to Move doll with the same skin tone as the 1st Wave of Blue Top doll for a head swap, the blond Camping Fun- Rock Climber Barbie Made to Move is the perfect match.

SUSSED The Weird Would You Rather Card Game | Ages: Teens, Adults, Kids 12+ | 110 Cards | for Family, Friends and More | Fantasy Version This is the third Sussed game that I've reviewed recently, and my second favorite. This one in particular has the highest age range of the three games, going 12-100, which is a little high, although I do believe the clues are a little more difficult to decipher in this set than the others, which I figured should range at the 7 or 8 to adult age range.

This set is far more thematic than the others, having clues that very specifically fit into the theme - adventure, fantasy, sci-fi and superheroes - which is a good concept. Other sets have tried this, but didn't have enough questions to ensure that the theme carried through.

It's a good get-to-know-you game with a definite shelf life based on the limited numbers of cards in the box and the nature of players to discuss. And this is also the game's strength - you will be talking with your family or friends or colleagues as you play. You just might not be able to play this one as infinitely as you may want.

text_fidelity_a:
Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 + I had a light bright as a kid, it wasn't a favorite toy of mine but it was pretty invigorating - I might've used it only a couple of times. That thing seemed like a tank. I guess it had to be to protect the bulb. You could even buy a replacement bulb if it broke.

This one sadly feels a bit cold and inexpensively made. No glowing filament bulb to keep things warm. Nice, new energy efficient electronics that are powered by 3 AAA batteries - hopefully you have some rechargeable ones to use.

The kickstand is terrible. You either have to hold it or lay it flat to put the pegs in but even then it rocks side to side easily. When you use the kickstand a slight bump to the top of the unit could knock it over.

The bezel is also too wide and I also don't understand the reason for the extended parts of the black plastic on the side. With such a wide bezel you don't need them and it would like nicer as a square.

My unit does not glow evenly. I opened it to see if something wasn't working. Everything was but there just weren't enough lights, one more and a little adjustment would've helped. The unit is also on a timer. As it runs on batteries having it lit all the time would likely drain them. They should have added a USB port and just not included the cable. You're not able to keep it powered on 24/7. It's maybe a 10 minute timer. Pressing the button multiple times changes the light mode: lit, 3 section rotating flashing light show, full on off blink and the last one turns the 4 LEDs on 1 at a time and then off 1 at a time.

I made one of the provided examples and I had just enough pegs of a few colors. a few extras would been nice.

The sticker on mine was very crooked and out of place.

However, where the LEDs do light the unit right, it does look cool. I think, way better than the OG, they're more neon glow, the colors are much better, instead of a yellow glow the LEDs are bright white which allows you to have yellow, pink, orange, blue and white pegs. These colors on the dark background are nice.
The pegs stay in nicely. I've only made one picture but not one has fallen out. It may not hold up to repeated removing and placing of the pegs but I plan on leaving it with a certain design for a while.

This would be awesome if it just had a few improvements. I'd probably buy another

Hasbro, you can do better than this. For an MSRP of $19.99 it's not worth it. Even Amazon's marked down price is too high. This is something I'd expect to see at 5 and below.
text_fidelity_b: Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 +

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+

text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Turbo Slam My feelings about this product are mixed -- We've long been fans of Scrabble, and thought we'd shake things up a bit by trying a different variation of the game. The Electronic Turbo Slam device, first required (3)- AAA batteries (not included). The device, when slammed has pretty loud sound effects/music, which I found annoying after a short while. I also thought there was too much commotion for me with everyone trying to slap down cards to change the letters, and I wasn't crazy about making just (4) letter words. As an adult, baby boomer, I much prefer the standard game of Scrabble -- quiet, relaxed and educational, and with more word potential.

I can see that this would be a great game for parents to play with young children to help them get interested in learning new words -- I would use it as an educational tool, instead of having them feel pressured to make words at record speed.

On the other hand, the speed and noise factor, would probably appeal to lots of teens. Overall, the game is relatively inexpensive, and worth a try for families who enjoy word faster paced, action filled games.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Turbo Slam

AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old LEGO have been hit by the inflation bug, and they've upped their prices recently on all sets. Nowhere is that more clear than in this set, which is very expensive for what you get.

Targeted towards the younger audience who is just beyond Duplo blocks, this is a pretty simple set with a pretty doofy-looking dragon that clearly skews younger, and doesn't fit in well with the rest of the Ninjago line, which is undoubtedly the LEGO line that has the highest "cool factor". So to judge this against a regular Ninjago set, this set woudl be a clear loser.

But it's really not for the older kids who can handle a ninja base or a 900-piece battle wagon, it's for littles. And for them, this is a fun set, but it is outrageously priced for what you get. It's essentially a few minifigs, a small dragon, a small set-piece, and a motorbike. Its simple to put together, but if you're working with a 4-year old, you probably need a little parental assistance.

For mini-munchkins, I suppose this would be a fun set to play with, but at close to $50 at the time of this writing, you are paying a very pretty penny for the fun you can have with it. At half that cost, and for the right audience, I'd find it a 4-star value. For what it is, I can't rank it higher than 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Forces & Interactions: Middle School Classroom Kit | NGSS-Aligned for Physics & Engineering Classes| Teacher Guide & Lesson Plans | Durable, Timed for Classroom Use, Includes Storage I generally love Thames and Kosovo’s products. This is a classroom physics kit. There are enough pieces to build several cars at once, but some experiments can only be done one at a time. For me that is fine since I am using this with homeschooling several kids, but for a small classroom, I can see students wanting to make their own. I am also not sure there are enough pieces to build more than one ramp. The snap pieces can be hard to remove especially for smaller finger, there is one connector puller included. For bigger groups of students I would have liked more of the pullers (looks a bit like the Lego splitter tool) You will need to provide weights for one experiment and batteries for the power module. I used slightly stronger nylon cord for my bucket pulls. It comes with magnets, wires, cord, nails, a cheep compass, and paper clips. Most of the odds and ends I just used my own and left the nails etc in the bucket.
There is a nice top divided tray to store the tinier pieces, and the bottom bin I left filled with the large pieces. The top of the storage box is dimpled to allow connecting the (not Lego) plastic building blocks to it. My kids had fun and easily figured out how to build onto any experiment we tried.
My one and biggest complaint with the kit is the magnet and iron filing board. None of the magnets work. They appear to have either been super heated or smacked around enough to unalign or weaken the magnet. I have a collection of bar magnets and rare earth magnets so I replaced the included magnets with my own. Most science teachers I know have collections of magnets so overall not a big issue. The clear iron filing board designed to show magnetic fields was a bust though. It’s not that the filings didn’t align, but that there were so few filings inside to show anything to begin with. I have a board I bought from a science teaching supply store and it has enough filings to demonstrate the magnetic field. This one was meh at best.
Because it does allow for multiple fun interactive classroom experiments I am rating this four stars. The spiral teaching book was great with Detailed instructions for building, and alignment guides (this assumes a knowledge of the material on the teacher’s part). The plastic technic like pieces were easy to use and fun for the kids. It was in the magnetism and wires and accessories that fell short of expectation. My Dad was a physicist (and MD) and I have a background in Physics as well, I had no trouble explaining what was going on to my kids, but this does not have answers to the questions because it assumes teacher knows answers, and how to relate NGSS Standards. Booklet includes lesson plan with target student age, time to teach, and any any materials needed. It is a great classroom kit, or group science instruction kit. Just keep in mind it’s target is classroom supplementary instruction, not home so kit is not designed to be a done by a kid on their own following a visually interesting book. (The spiral is pretty standard for teacher lesson books)
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Forces & Interactions: Middle School Classroom Kit | NGSS-Aligned for Physics & Engineering Classes| Teacher Guide & Lesson Plans | Durable, Timed for Classroom Use, Includes Storage

Snap Circuits Classic SC-300 Electronics Exploration Kit | Over 300 Projects | Full Color Manual Parts | STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8+ 2.3 x 13.6 x 19.3 inches I got this kit for my 10 year old. We had been experimenting with kit electric motors, magnets and radios and everything ended up mixed in a box that he liked to play with, so there was interest in this type of toy.

The parts of this kit snap together on a clear plastic grid. The instruction book is a black and white center stapled pamphlet that can be challenging to decipher for builds that are more complex. My son liked building the simple circuit that included the motor with the fan. Many of the advanced plans are very similar.

The kit seems durable but not indestructable. My kids can be pretty rough on things so they have been using this kit with my supervision.

For most kids under 10, this is not the type of toy that they can play with on their own. I have my son use this toy at the dining room table. We check to make sure that all of the parts get back in their place when we are done.

This is an educational toy. My experience is that early exposure to learning experiences like this can shape interests later on in life.

I would have liked to have seen a description of what the various modules do to the electricity to make the magic happen.

If you have any specific questions please leave a comment and I'll try to get back to you as soon as I can.
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Classic SC-300 Electronics Exploration Kit | Over 300 Projects | Full Color Manual Parts | STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8+ 2.3 x 13.6 x 19.3 inches

Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+ We are really loving these Hot Dots learning activity books. My preschooler loves to count, so this math book is great for getting some counting practice in. I never worked on pattern recognition, and this book includes that, so I’m so glad we’re getting some exposure with that (i.e. circle, circle, square, circle, circle —insert what comes next). It also covers big and small, shapes, the most and the least themes, heavy and light, as well as matching. There’s a lot to learn in this workbook, and it’s a lot of fun.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+

Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall) This unyielding, oversized beast hangs out in my daughter's room and watches her while she sleeps. It has given me pause a couple of times because it has a very serious, fierce Cheetah face. Angry even. This isn't your garden variety Beanie Boo or cute puffy kitty plush. This is a predator and it lets you know it.

Way back when I was a kid, back when we wore newspapers around our feet instead of shoes to trudge to school in 18 feet of snow, I had a panther like this. It was all black and scary enough to send the house cat running full speed out of the room with a puffy tail. I loved my Bagheera so dearly, like my daughter loves this Cheetah. Some sort of magic happens when little girls receive a giant stuffed cat for the Christmas of their 8th year. Alas, my Bagheera crossed the stuffed animal Rainbow Bridge many years ago, but he will always be fondly remembered.

I am very happy that my daughter is also able to shower her love on a giant, regal stuffed animal like I did as a kid, when we lived without electricity or indoor toilets, and my only source of heat was snuggling with my stuffed wild cat. I always took my Bagheera to the outhouse with me in the dead on the night to scare off the wolves, coyotes, and wild boar. That I am here writing this today is evidence that my stuffed cat had a huge impact on my young life. I have no doubt that this Cheetah would also do a great job of deterring bears and badgers on a late night stroll to use the toilet. Thankfully my daughter will never have to deal with such harrowing circumstances, but nevertheless, even if its only job is to sit in a room looking majestic, I highly recommend that you gift this Cheetah to a lucky kid.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall)

text_fidelity_a:
All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions [[VIDEOID:moOM6Q7TMDWRNW]]This is like an awesome mix between Apples to Apples and Trivial Pursuit. It's played very similarly to Apples to Apples, but you have an open-ended question, and everyone writes answers down on a piece of paper. Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

Pros:
+Awesome questions
+Fun game
+Good quality
+Well designed

Cons:
-You need 4 people to play according to the rules, even though these are fun questions to ask if there are just two or three of you
text_fidelity_b: All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

Speaking of which, the big dog and cats love it too.  The toy moves better than you'd think, and it's every bit as durable as you'd like.  It does get stuck along the wall or fall over, but it keeps going.  Carpet doesn't work nearly as well as harder surfaces.  I wouldn't recommend it for carpet (unless the dense hard stuff). The bright colors and ever present Mickey marketing seem to help keep the kids going as well.  As noted in another review, this isn't really interactive or educational, but it's a fine toy.

HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 This is a great little plane, no question. But I ignored Hobbyzone's recommendation for 14 years old and up. I bought two: one for each of my 9-year-old twin sons, who were hot to fly RC model airplanes. One learned to fly quickly, but the other has been seriously disappointed. And I had to learn quickly how to use styrofoam glue to reattach broken wings, tail parts, motor mounts, etc.

It took me a while to understand how critical the trim really is: a beginner really can't fly a plane that isn't trimmed properly. You can get the trim in the ballpark with visual inspection of the control surfaces, but to get it right you have to fly the plane yourself. When I did that, and touched up the trim, flying became a lot of fun - for one boy. The other boy still can't fly more than a few seconds before landing his plane on its nose. He has just about given up in disgust.

I suspect that in a year or two both boys will have good flying skills. But in the meantime one boy is ready to move up while the other is ready to give up. Bummer!
text_fidelity_b: HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900

text_fidelity_a: Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on My toddler is really into Mickey right now so I just had to get him this trike. It’s adorable and super well made. Assembly was straightforward, thanks to clear and helpful instructions. It took me about half an hour to put together but my toddler was “helping” me so it really wouldn’t take quite that long. I really appreciate the design of this trike since it’s made to grow with your child. It starts out with safety straps, bars that lock in as a secondary way to keep your child in the seat and a handle so you can push and steer. There’s a switch on the front wheel that you slide so it will move without the pedals. Once your child gets big enough to ride alone, move the switch back and the front wheel is controlled by the pedals. The handle is removable as are the safety bars and canopy. I always love finding toys that will get a lot of use since there are so many things that are really only made for short time periods or specific developmental stages then they’re quickly outgrown. This is a wonderful toy and I’m looking forward to helping my son learn to ride it as he grows.
text_fidelity_b: Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on
